providers.title: Unitarizable representations
providers.scope: A uniformly bounded representation is similar to a unitary one iff a bounded Q with a <= Q <= b (a > 0) satisfies pi(g)^* Q pi(g) = Q for all g, iff it preserves an equivalent inner product.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Amenable groups are unitarizable (Day, Dixmier)
providers.scope: Every uniformly bounded representation of an amenable discrete group on a Hilbert space is similar to a unitary representation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Triangular representations
providers.scope: A bounded operator cocycle D for a unitary representation U gives the representation [[U, DU], [0, U]] with norms at most 1 + ||D(g)||; if it is unitarizable, D is inner.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Induction from a subgroup
providers.scope: A uniformly bounded representation of a subgroup K induces one of G on l^2(G/K; E) with the same uniform bound; if the induced representation is unitarizable, so is the original.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finitely generated subgroups and amenability
providers.scope: If every finitely generated subgroup is amenable, the group is amenable; a nonamenable group has a finitely generated nonamenable subgroup.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A contracting average
providers.scope: A countable nonamenable group has a finite S containing e with ||(1/|S|) sum over t in S of R_t|| < 1 on l^2(G).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hall's theorem, countable form
providers.scope: If X is countable, every N(x) is finite and |N(F)| >= |F| for every finite F, there is an injective choice phi(x) in N(x) on all of X (the finite case, Lemma 2.1, by augmenting paths).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sparse assignment
providers.scope: The d^l products s_i of words of length l in S admit a: G x [n] -> {0,1} with at most r = ceil(n rho^l) ones at every row x and at most r zeros among the edges (y s_i^(-1), i) at every column y.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sums of random signs
providers.scope: For independent uniform signs, P(|sum c_i eps_i| > u) <= 2 exp(-u^2 / (2 sum c_i^2)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nets on spheres
providers.scope: The unit sphere of R^m has a 1/4-net with at most 9^m points (volume comparison).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Random sign frames
providers.scope: There are n unit vectors in C^k, k = ceil(2r log 2n), such that every subfamily of at most min(2r, n) of them has synthesis operator of norm at most 10.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Masked operator estimate
providers.scope: If every row and every column of a mask carries at most p labels and all synthesis operators of at most p of the vectors have norm at most b_0, the masked operator has norm at most b_0^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform conjugation differences
providers.scope: For the operator T of a sparse assignment, ||T - U(g) T U(g)^(-1)|| <= 100 for every g; the block rows of T and the block columns of A - T also have norm at most 100 (Corollary 3.1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kernel energy
providers.scope: The translation-invariant operator A has kernel W(s) = sum of P_i over s_i = s, with Hilbert-Schmidt energy at least n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Distance from the translation commutant
providers.scope: If A commutes with translations and has kernel energy E, T has row at e and A - T column at e of norm at most K, then every C in the commutant satisfies E <= 4k(K + ||T - C||)^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direct-sum obstruction
providers.scope: Uniform bounds K on rows, columns and conjugation differences with E_j / k_j -> infinity give a non-unitarizable representation with norms at most 1 + K on a separable space.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Unitarizable groups are amenable (OpenAI; Dixmier's question)
providers.scope: A discrete group is amenable iff unitarizable; a nonamenable group has non-unitarizable representations with all norms at most 1 + eps, on a separable space if the group is countable.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Thompson's group F
providers.scope: Thompson's group F has non-unitarizable representations with all norms at most 1 + eps on a separable space.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Group C*-algebras
providers.scope: For a non-unitarizable uniformly bounded representation, the bounded homomorphism T_pi of l^1(G) has no bounded unital homomorphic extension to C*(G) or C*_r(G) (via Kadison's similarity theorem).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
